title: A Vow for the Promise
premise: Emrys Ashgrove, a ghostwriter hiding from a scandal that destroyed his old name, is hired to write the memoirs of vintner Marguerite Vale—only to discover her orchard deed legally entangles his estranged family, whose vineyard borders hers. As he shuttles between two households that hate each other over a decades-old betrayal, Emrys must decide whether to expose the truth in the memoir or bury it to protect the fragile belonging he's found. When the deed dispute erupts into litigation on the eve of first harvest, Emrys chooses truth at the cost of both clients' trust, confessing his own buried role in the original betrayal. The novel ends at harvest: the memoir published under his real name, the orchard divided but shared, and Emrys forgiven—by Marguerite, by his family, and finally by himself.
about_author: Beatrix Iversen is a former sommelier who left the restaurant world to write about love, land, and the lies families tell themselves. She lives among the orchards of the Pacific Northwest, where she keeps a stubborn half-acre of apples no one asked for.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Manuscript
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Emrys accepts a lucrative commission from vintner Marguerite Vale, concealing his identity behind his ghostwriting alias. Reviewing her estate papers, he finds a deed naming both Vale and Ashgrove—his own family. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional calm; the past knocking before he's ready to answer.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Line
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. He visits the county records office and confirms the deed binds both properties through an unbroken covenant neither family can dissolve alone. His brother Callum refuses to discuss it by phone. Emotional beat: dread curdling into compulsion—the safe life measured in small steps begins to crack.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Version
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Interviewing Marguerite for the memoir, Emrys hears her account of the betrayal: an Ashgrove broke a promise that cost her father the harvest of '98. She's warm, sharp, and grieving. Emotional beat: seduction of belonging—he starts wanting to be seen by her, which terrifies him.

chapters.title: Callum's Version
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. At the Ashgrove vineyard, Callum tells the opposite story, and their father's silence hangs over the table. Emrys realizes both families are protecting someone. Emotional beat: loyalty pulling against truth; he catches himself editing reality the way he edits manuscripts.

chapters.title: What the Ghost Wrote
chapters.summary: POV: Marguerite. Reading Emrys's draft chapters, Marguerite senses a writer who knows too much about shame. She confronts him gently; he deflects with craft. Meanwhile she reveals the covenant requires both signatures—and both truths—to break. Emotional beat: intimacy deepening on a foundation of concealment.

chapters.title: The Father's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Emrys finds his late father's ledger proving the Ashgroves knowingly falsified the '98 harvest records to save their own vines, framing Marguerite's father. Callum begs him to burn it. Emotional beat: the mirror moment—Emrys sees his own cowardice reflected in his father's choices.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Lawyers descend; Marguerite discovers Emrys's real name and realizes her ghostwriter is the son of the man who ruined her family. She dismisses him. Emotional beat: devastation and clarity—staying invisible cost him everything visible.

chapters.title: The Confession Draft
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Alone, Emrys writes the true final chapter of the memoir—naming his father's crime and his own five years of complicit silence—and sends it to Marguerite unsigned, then signs it. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve; forgiveness of self begins with testimony.

chapters.title: First Pressing
chapters.summary: POV: Marguerite. On harvest day, Marguerite reads the confession as pickers work the rows. She arrives at the Ashgrove crush pad with the ledger and the deed, offering co-signature—not absolution, but a future. Emotional beat: hard-won grace; trust rebuilt on truth rather than comfort.

chapters.title: A Vow for the Promise
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. The covenant is dissolved and rewritten as a shared stewardship agreement; the memoir publishes under Emrys Ashgrove's name. At the harvest supper, Callum pours the first joint vintage, and Marguerite takes Emrys's hand. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not inherited—the vow finally kept.
